Director of Technology- Process Development & Scale-Up

ElementUSA is seeking a Director of Technology – Process Development & Scale-Up to provide technical leadership across the development, scale-up, and commercialization of novel mineral and materials processing technologies. This role will lead and challenge multidisciplinary technical teams working across both hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical processes, ensuring laboratory and pilot development is focused not only on technical performance, but also on scalability, operability, economics, and commercial execution.

The Director will work closely with PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, process engineers, project managers, operations personnel, equipment suppliers, and external engineering partners to translate experimental results into maturing process flowsheets, design criteria, equipment requirements, and engineering packages.

A critical responsibility of this position will be establishing the technical-development management system that connects test campaigns, technical risks, pilot capabilities, process flowsheet maturity, engineering requirements, and scale-up decisions.

Technology & Process Development
Provide technical leadership across hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical process-development programs.
Lead, mentor, manage, and constructively challenge PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, and process-development personnel.
Review test campaigns to ensure clear objectives, hypotheses, success criteria, priorities, and actionable outcomes.
Challenge assumptions and results related to mass balances, recoveries, selectivity, reagent consumption, impurity behavior, energy requirements, process conditions, and scalability.
Drive maturation of integrated process flowsheets from laboratory concepts through pilot-scale demonstration and commercial readiness.
Identify critical technical unknowns and develop structured test programs to systematically retire technical and scale-up risks.
Ensure development work generates the data required for engineering design, economic evaluation, and commercial decision-making.

Technology Development Governance & Execution
Establish and maintain a practical management system for technology and process-development activities across laboratory, pilot, and scale-up programs.
Develop and manage KPIs, scorecards, trackers, and review cadences that provide clear visibility into technical progress, priorities, risks, decisions, and next steps.
Maintain an integrated view of active and planned test campaigns, including objectives, technical questions, success criteria, owners, schedules, results, conclusions, and follow-up actions.
Ensure testing is tied to specific flowsheet decisions, technical risks, scale-up requirements, engineering inputs, or economic assumptions rather than testing for testing's sake.
Develop and maintain a technical risk and unknowns register with defined test plans for retiring critical uncertainties.
Develop a pilot equipment and capability roadmap identifying what equipment is required, why it is needed, which test or scale-up objective it supports, timing, cost, and readiness.
Challenge proposed pilot equipment purchases to ensure capital is aligned with the process-development and commercialization roadmap.
Track technology maturity by major unit operation from concept to laboratory proof, pilot demonstration, engineering design basis, commissioning, and operations.
Establish technical readiness criteria and stage gates for advancing technologies into the next phase.
Lead recurring technology reviews focused on results, risks, decisions, priorities, and next experiments rather than activity reporting.
Provide the COO and executive leadership with a concise view of technical maturity, unresolved risks, upcoming decisions, resource requirements, and readiness for scale-up.

Scale-Up & Engineering Translation
Serve as a primary technical bridge between process development and engineering execution teams.
Translate laboratory and pilot results into process design criteria, mass and energy balances, process flow diagrams, equipment requirements, operating parameters, and other engineering inputs.
Work closely with project management and engineering teams to ensure technology packages are sufficiently mature before advancing into detailed engineering and capital execution.
Participate in equipment specification, vendor technical evaluations, pilot equipment selection, engineering reviews, and design decisions.
Clearly distinguish what has been demonstrated, what remains uncertain, and what additional testing is required before design assumptions are frozen.
Understand and support the progression from concept and FEL/design through procurement, construction, commissioning, startup, and steady-state operations.
Remain engaged through engineering, commissioning, and startup to ensure process-development intent is successfully translated into operating equipment.

Techno-Economic & Commercialization Support
Incorporate economic thinking throughout process development rather than treating economics as a downstream activity.
Evaluate process decisions considering recovery, selectivity, reagent consumption, energy demand, throughput, equipment requirements, waste generation, recycle streams, CAPEX, and OPEX implications.
Work with Engineering, Operations, Finance, and leadership to identify the major technical and economic drivers affecting commercial viability.
Help establish technical and economic stage gates for advancing technologies from laboratory development through pilot and commercial scale.
Identify development pathways that may be technically achievable but commercially impractical and recommend alternatives.

Pilot & Operations Support
Support commissioning, startup, troubleshooting, and optimization of pilot and demonstration equipment.
Ensure lessons learned during pilot operations are captured and incorporated into future process and engineering designs.
Partner with Operations to establish operating windows, critical process parameters, sampling requirements, process controls, and operating procedures.
Support root-cause analysis and technical troubleshooting as technologies transition from development into continuous operation.
Maintain a strong connection between laboratory development and real-world plant operability, maintainability, safety, reliability, and workforce requirements.

Leadership & Organization Development
Manage and develop a multidisciplinary technical organization that may include PhD scientists, metallurgists, chemists, process engineers, laboratory personnel, and technical specialists.
Establish clear priorities, accountability, development objectives, and technical ownership across the team.
Create a culture where technical assumptions are constructively challenged and decisions are driven by data.
Balance scientific exploration with schedule, cost, commercialization priorities, and company objectives.
Develop technical talent and organizational capability as the company progresses from early-stage process development into commercial operations.

Candidate Profile
Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Mineral Processing, Extractive Metallurgy, or a related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
Significant industrial experience across both hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy, ideally involving mineral processing, extractive metallurgy, critical minerals, metals refining, recycling, or related process industries.
Demonstrated experience developing and scaling processes from laboratory through pilot and/or commercial operation.
Strong understanding of hydrometallurgical operations such as leaching, precipitation, filtration, solvent extraction, ion exchange, crystallization, and solid/liquid separation.
Strong understanding of pyrometallurgical operations such as reduction, roasting, calcination, furnaces, thermal processing, gas handling, and solids processing.
Demonstrated ability to lead, manage, mentor, and challenge highly technical scientists and PhD-level personnel.
Experience developing process flowsheets, mass balances, design criteria, process-engineering deliverables, and structured technical-development programs.
Working knowledge of capital project development and engineering execution, including stage-gate/FEL processes, project management, equipment specification, vendor engagement, engineering reviews, commissioning, and startup.
Strong understanding of the relationship between process performance and commercial economics.
Demonstrated people-management experience and ability to build high-performing technical teams.
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate highly technical information into clear recommendations for executive leadership, engineering, operations, and commercial stakeholders.

Join Us

If you’re excited by the idea of advancing sustainable mineral science and want your analytical work to make a measurable impact, we’d love to hear from you.
